acceptance: exactly one code-to-UX policy table exists; no component maps a code to copy, retry-ness, or escalation on its own
no raw error text is rendered — every user-facing error string resolves from the table via an i18n key, never a raw error.message or status
every data view renders through the state-dispatcher (loading -> error -> empty -> data); a 200-with-no-rows renders the empty branch; no raw I/O in render

the classified error is drawn by the one shared error-tile renderer, which alone owns the session-end escalation (the escalation call appears only inside that renderer) — conditional on a session/auth concept
every render-throwing subtree sits inside a boundary at its tier; one failing block never blanks its siblings or the page
when boundaries nest, the nearest enclosing one handles the throw; the outer floor catches only escapes no inner boundary caught
a bounded subtree that threw exposes a retry/recover affordance where the code is retryable, without a full page reload
exactly one outermost floor catches what route-level boundaries cannot, including throws in the app shell (above the router if the app has one)

each channel the app actually uses routes its error to the prescribed placement (render-throw -> boundary tile, query-error -> dispatcher tile, mutation-error -> toast, loader/action -> route error element, uncaught async -> floor); unused channels are exempt
behaviour is policy-driven — retry is offered only for reasons the table marks retryable, redirect/sign-out only for auth/session reasons; no component hardcodes a retry button
the architecture test: adding a brand-new error code touches only the policy table and its i18n keys — zero component changes
